chapter: New Orleans teachers and classical musicians
title: Concert halls and classical players who also played jazz
summary: Concerts were held in halls with paid admission; the same classical players could play jazz melodically, Gaspard picking bass beautifully.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well I was going to ask these concerts at the Keough and all of them, Dave, where would they be? What kind of an auditorium?
Well they had it in the, in the, uh, Narkeeson Hall, Franz Ami Hall. North Carolina Hall. Yes, they had it. And you pay so much to go in.

Enjoy that music, that classic, that high class stuff. But them same guys can come out and get in the orchestra and play jazz music too. But they play that melody. You see, they were used to playing melodies. They let the people understand what they were doing. You have to look, sometime I look, I saw, when I saw old man, uh, Gaspar, old Gaspar playing in an orchestra. And they give them choruses. And he talk about picking bass violin. He picked it beautiful. You wouldn't hear the string hit up against the finger roll. Beautiful. Jazz too. I think that's going in the machine.

Hold on, I don't hurt, the storm won't hurt that I don't think. Well, that kind of... Instead of picking up all the rain, you hear the rain on here and the, uh, thunder. I guess that won't be the tornado they predicted maybe anyway, we hope not.
